item.title: Conservative activists posing as Minnesota voters at polling places could be in legal trouble
item.description: Members of the Florida-based conservative activist group Citizen Justice League were seen in an undercover video, posing in what they called Muslim costumes and pretending to be Minnesota voters looking for vouchers. The stunt could land them in serious legal trouble. CBS News' Esme Murphy reports.

item.title: Klarna posts shocking revenue jump
item.description: "Buy now, pay later" company Klarna posted a shocking 27% revenue jump between April and June 2026. Stacy Cowley, a business reporter for The New York Times, breaks it down.

item.title: Trump says no talks with Iran ongoing, and none scheduled
item.description: President Trump says the U.S. is not engaged in any talks with Iran as the two countries remain locked in a standoff over the Strait of Hormuz after almost six months of war.

item.title: Trump says Strait of Hormuz is "open and operating." Shipping data appears to contradict his claim.
item.description: President Trump said on social media Tuesday that no talks or conversations are underway with Iran and that the Strait of Hormuz is "open and operating." However, shipping data says otherwise. CBS News' Natalie Brand has more.

item.title: Disney and ABC sue FCC over early license review, alleging retaliation
item.description: The lawsuit comes after the FCC ordered ABC to seek renewals between two and five years before its TV stations' licenses were set to expire.

item.title: Meta's federal trial begins over child social media addiction claims
item.description: The lawsuit accuses the social media giant of contributing to the youth mental health crisis by deliberately designing features that addict children to its platforms.

item.title: Madonna leads 2026 MTV VMAs with 11 nominations
item.description: Madonna leads all artists with 11 nominations at this year's MTV VMAs, and a full sweep would tie her with Beyoncé and Taylor Swift for the most VMA wins in history.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy admitted to killing her children. Why are true crime fans saying she didn't?
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial is generating endless discussion among true crime aficionados online, sparking theories and misinformation over the case. Kathryn Coduto, an assistant professor of media sciences at Boston University, explains why the case has taken social media by storm.

item.title: Watch Live: Former mother-in-law says Lindsay Clancy was "begging for help"
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial​ resumed Tuesday in Massachusetts with the 15th day of testimony.

item.title: Why four states are suing Meta in landmark trial
item.description: Opening arguments begin Tuesday in a landmark trial where four states are suing Meta for alleged mental health harm and addictive design. CBS News contributor Rebecca Roiphe has the latest.

item.title: Judge blocks plan to move FBI headquarters
item.description: A judge blocked a Trump administration plan to move the FBI headquarters to Washington, D.C.

item.title: Appeals court upholds block on immigration arrests at certain houses of worship
item.description: A federal appeals court sided with houses of worship from the Quaker, Sikh, and Cooperative Baptist Fellowship religious traditions.

item.title: Justice Department to send a record 1,000 monitors to midterm polling places
item.description: The Justice Department is planning to deploy a record 1,000 federal monitors to polling places throughout the U.S. for the midterm elections.

item.title: Human remains found in Lake Mead as water levels reach record low
item.description: The skeletal remains were found on Sunday, two years after similar drought conditions exposed bodies in the lake.

item.title: Will mortgage rates drop below 6% in 2026?
item.description: A lot of conditions must shift for mortgage rates to fall.

item.title: Ukraine targets Moscow with drones as Russia threatens U.K. over support
item.description: Ukraine targets Moscow with a huge wave of drones as Russia warns the U.K. will pay a price for supplying Kyiv with long-range weapons.

item.title: Supply chain issues contributing to poor conditions aboard the USS Lincoln, reporter claims
item.description: President Trump is pushing back against reports of dismal conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, which has been at sea longer than usual for a military vessel. Military Times Pentagon correspondent Natalie Oliverio spoke with the families of soldiers aboard.

item.title: Suge Knight could be a hostile witness at Tupac Shakur murder trial, lawyer says
item.description: More witnesses will testify at the trial against the man accused of calling the shots in the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur. CBS News legal contributor Caroline Polisi has the latest details.

item.title: Data centers and AI become huge issue for midterm elections voters
item.description: Artificial intelligence and the data centers powering the technology have become a flashpoint ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Shira Ovide, a technology reporter for The Wall Street Journal, has more.

item.title: Torrential rain prolongs flood conditions in the Midwest and North Carolina
item.description: Homes and infrastructure were destroyed by flooding in parts of the Midwest and North Carolina. CBS News' Tom Hanson reports, and Rob Marciano has the forecast.

item.title: Floridians duke it out in gubernatorial primary
item.description: CBS News political director Fin Gómez takes a tour through the major primaries to watch this week.

item.title: Watch: Lindsay Clancy's former mother-in-law testifies she was "begging for help"
item.description: Lindsay Clancy's former mother-in-law, Susan Clancy, told the courtroom on Tuesday that her former daughter-in-law was "begging for help" during postpartum.

item.title: DOJ to stop using outside experts to help vet competitive grant applicants
item.description: The Justice Department is scrapping its longtime practice of hiring outside experts to help review competitive grant applications, multiple sources told CBS News.

item.title: Florida voters choose in governor, Senate primaries, and more races to watch
item.description: Three states are holding primaries on Tuesday, with Florida deciding on nominees for both governor and for Senate.

item.title: USS Benfold went days without power in the South China Sea
item.description: The guided-missile destroyer USS Benfold spent four days without power last month after a problem with its engineering, according to a spokesperson for the Navy's 7th Fleet.

item.title: Trump says no Iran talks are planned or ongoing and claims the Strait of Hormuz is open
item.description: President Trump admitted that the U.S. and Iran have no ongoing or planned negotiations right now. Meanwhile, Jared Kushner met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the fate of Gaza. CBS News' Nancy Cordes reports.

item.title: Outshine Fruit Bars recalled over possible glass, parent Dreyer's says
item.description: Five flavors of Outshine Fruit Bars sold nationwide were recalled because they may include glass, Dreyer's Grand Ice Cream said.

item.title: Newsom may veto bill giving California high-speed rail watchdog more power, sources say
item.description: Critics called it the "anti-transparency" bill. Newsom quietly enacted the controversial part and may now veto the part the rail watchdog says he needs, sources tell CBS California.

item.title: Judge blocks plan to move FBI headquarters to Reagan Building
item.description: U.S. District Judge Theodore Chuang ruled that the Trump administration's move to divert funding and cancel a plan to move the FBI to Maryland was "arbitrary and capricious and not in accordance with law."

item.title: U.S.-Iran ceasefire holds for now, Hegseth says, as Trump looks to finalize deal
item.description: Hegseth said the ceasefire with Iran "certainly holds" for now after a naval clash between Iranian and U.S. forces and renewed attacks on the UAE.
